meta.title: Viollet
meta.description: How I built an AI-assisted personal finance product that turns bank email notifications into categorized spending without bank credentials or manual entry.
meta.role: Solo builder, from architecture through production

hero.summary: Viollet is a side project I designed and built end to end. It connects Gmail, ingests bank transaction notifications, categorizes spending with AI, and surfaces budgets and insights without asking for online banking credentials.

context.title: 1. Context
paragraphs: Most personal finance apps still depend on manual logging or direct bank integrations that are hard to ship, expensive to maintain, and often unavailable for regional banks.

In the Dominican Republic, many people already receive credit, debit, and transfer alerts by email. The product opportunity was to meet users where their data already lives: turn those notifications into structured transactions, categories, and spending views with zero manual entry.

constraints.title: 2. Constraints
paragraphs: Viollet is a solo side project, so scope had to stay focused on one reliable ingestion path instead of building a full open-banking platform on day one.

Financial data raised the bar for security and trust: no bank passwords, read-only Gmail access with explicit user consent, and a codebase that stays private while the product is still in public beta.
bullets: No bank credential collection, only email notifications the user already receives
Gmail restricted scopes require Google verification and ongoing security review
Bank notification formats vary across 15+ Dominican institutions and differ by card vs. account
Storage uses Turso with Drizzle, not a generic SQLite label

responsibility.title: 3. My responsibility
paragraphs: I owned the product from problem framing through production: system boundaries, data model, Gmail/OAuth flow, webhook ingestion, AI-assisted categorization, dashboard UX, and deployment.

That included choosing what to automate first (email-based capture and categorization), what to defer (direct bank APIs), and how to explain trade-offs clearly on the public site so users understand access and revocation.

architecture.title: 4. Architecture
paragraphs: The runtime has three cooperating paths: the signed-in Next.js app on Vercel (Clerk for sessions), asynchronous mail ingestion (Gmail watch plus a Pub/Sub push into a webhook route), and Drizzle on Turso for the ledger.

A supported notification is cleaned, extracted with the AI SDK into a typed object (through the Vercel AI Gateway in production), categorized, and stored. The dashboard and the assistant read those rows for budgets, trends, and answers.
architecture.diagramCaption: Choose a node to see how Gmail, Pub/Sub, Next.js, Clerk, Vercel, the AI SDK, and Turso split the work.

items.decision: Email notifications instead of bank APIs
items.rationale: Bank APIs and aggregators would expand coverage faster in theory, but they add partnership overhead and uneven regional support. Email alerts are already delivered to users and let Viollet ship a working beta without storing banking credentials.

items.decision: Turso + Drizzle for the data layer
items.rationale: A managed libSQL edge database keeps operational overhead low for a solo builder while Drizzle gives typed schema migrations and queries. The trade-off is designing ingestion to be idempotent and webhook-safe rather than relying on a single monolithic worker.

Pure rules break when banks change templates or wording. The AI SDK helps classify ambiguous merchants and categories, with parsing constraints to keep outputs structured. The trade-off is monitoring quality and keeping prompts focused on financial metadata, not general inbox content.

Clerk reduced time-to-ship for session management and let me focus engineering time on Gmail sync and ingestion reliability. The trade-off is coupling auth to a hosted provider, acceptable for a beta where speed and security defaults matter.

impact.title: 6. Impact
paragraphs: Viollet is live at viollet.app as a free public beta. Users connect Gmail, select authorized financial senders, and get automated expense tracking from notifications. This replaces manual logging for the supported flow.

Public product scope today includes support for 15+ Dominican banks and cards (with evaluation for additional institutions that send email alerts), plus budgets, spending trends, and proactive insights derived from categorized transactions.
bullets: Gmail → categorized spend automation with zero manual entry for connected accounts
No online banking usernames or passwords collected
Users can revoke Gmail access from Google or inside the product workflow

operationalQuality.title: 8. Operational quality
paragraphs: Because the product handles financial metadata, the implementation treats transport and storage carefully: encrypted data in transit and at rest, read-only Gmail scopes scoped to user-selected senders, and clear copy on the public site about Google's verification process for restricted permissions.

Ingestion is built for reliability at the webhook boundary: validate push deliveries, make writes idempotent where possible, and keep the parsing/categorization path isolated so a bad template does not corrupt unrelated user data.
bullets: Google app verification completed; restricted Gmail scopes follow Google's security assessment cycle
Public FAQ documents access, revocation, and data use without advertising resale
Webhook + Pub/Sub path decouples mail delivery from request/response UI latency

architecture.title: Inspect one piece
architecture.description: Hover or focus a node. Click to pin the explanation.

nodes.name: Gmail
nodes.summary: Read-only API. The grant is gmail.readonly. Viollet calls users.watch on INBOX and history.list with historyTypes messageAdded. It cannot send, delete, or edit mail.

nodes.name: Google Pub/Sub
nodes.summary: Gmail publishes mailbox changes to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic. The app does not poll for every new message. The webhook receives the historyId.

nodes.name: Next.js
nodes.summary: App Router, server actions, and the /api/gmail/webhook route. Sender filtering, extraction, and ledger writes are orchestrated here.

nodes.name: Vercel
nodes.summary: The app runs on Vercel. In production, email extraction goes through the Vercel AI Gateway. A Gemini model is the non-production fallback.

nodes.name: Clerk
nodes.summary: Sessions for the signed-in app. The Gmail token is a separate secret, encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it is stored. Clerk does not replace the Google grant.

nodes.name: AI SDK
nodes.summary: Extraction asks the AI SDK for an object validated with zod: type, amount in cents, merchant, account, category, and confidence. Deterministic rules can still correct withdrawals, card payments, and the person's own rules. A model category is accepted at confidence 85 or higher.

nodes.name: Turso
nodes.summary: libSQL through Drizzle. Emails, transactions, accounts, categories, institutions, and gmailSyncState live here. emails.gmailMessageId is unique, so a replayed push does not insert a second row.

parse.title: From alert to ledger row
parse.description: Step through one Banreservas notice from the landing demo. This simulates the production pipeline. It does not call Gmail or a model. The score of 92 is illustrative. The threshold of 85 is the one in the code.
parse.cleanedLabel: Clean text, with HTML and the legal footer removed.
parse.waiting: The row appears once extraction has an object.

steps.title: The alert arrives
steps.body: Banreservas sends an email. Merchant, card, and amount are still mixed into the prose. Nothing is in the ledger yet.

steps.title: The sender matches
steps.body: notificaciones@banreservas.com is a confirmed Banreservas sender. If this person had not authorized that bank, the message would be skipped.

steps.title: The text is cleaned
steps.body: HTML becomes text and legal footers are removed before the model sees the message. The model gets the financial notice, not the disclaimer.

steps.title: Structured extraction
steps.body: The AI SDK asks for an object: transaction type, amount in cents, merchant, account, and last four. DOP 2,591.00 becomes -259100 cents on Visa Premia ending 7392.

steps.title: The category is resolved
steps.body: Deterministic rules run first: the person's prompt rules, withdrawals, and payments to a card. None of those hit this sample. The illustrative confidence is 92, above the real accept threshold of 85, so Supermarkets is kept with source llm. Below that threshold Viollet checks the person's merchant map, then the global map. With no map, the category stays pending for enrichment.

steps.title: It is written once
steps.body: Drizzle inserts the email and the transaction in Turso. emails.gmailMessageId is unique and the insert uses onConflictDoNothing. A second delivery of the same Gmail id does not create another transaction.

sync.title: Watch, push, and a duplicate
sync.description: Run the actions in order. The log follows the real Gmail watch and webhook path, including the duplicate guard.

connect: Refresh token encrypted with AES-256-GCM. No bank password stored.
watch: gmail.users.watch on INBOX, publishing to the Cloud Pub/Sub topic.
gmailSyncState saved historyId and the watch expiration.
push: Push received at /api/gmail/webhook. Coalesced for 8 seconds, then processed.
history.list with historyTypes messageAdded returned one id.
Extraction wrote one email and one transaction. gmailMessageId is unique.
replay: The same history push arrived again.
